newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end down almost 1 pct in empty market.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end down almost 1 pct in empty market.

text.p: Dutch shares ended almost one percent lower on Thursday, but the AEX index held above the 700 mark, in a very thin market devoid of keen trading interest.
"There are no investors there. It's an empty market. The only people there are the ones who want to make a quick gamble on a certain situation," one trader said.
The AEX index ended down 6.44 points to 702.11, off the early session low of 698.05. Only four of the leading 25 shares rose. The rest fell.
Traders said the weakness of the market was a natural response to Wall Street's Wednesday night fall.
Some added the drop of June German bund futures below the 99.25/30 area had confirmed the weak tone.
"It broke that level and we saw all the equity markets across Europe coming off," one trader said.
Nevertheless, many traders remained bullish for the medium term, saying they saw stability or even gains once the short-term uncertainty over U.S. interest rates has passed.
"The retail side are not panicking. We will probably head down to 670/680 and see some buying, because all the fear will be out," one trader said.
On a day of general decline, few stocks stood out.
In late morning trading, ING provided a modest market prop, its shares rising as high as 70.80 after announcing a 25 percent rise of 1996 net profits, at the high end of analysts' estimates.
Traders and analysts agreed the figures were good. However, ING shares subsequently dropped back to 69.30, a one guilder loss on the day.

Some traders said the brief rise and fall was the result of short-term cash plays and light profit-taking thereafter. Others added end investors were already heavy with shares in the financial sector after its healthy run in the past year.
Among the modest gainers were business publishers Elsevier , up 20 cents to 29.50 guilders, and Wolters Kluwer , up 90 cents to 218.30 guilders.

Elsevier firmed after speculation arose that the company would shortly make an acquisition. The rumours circulated after the company on Tuesday filed a shelf with the SEC to sell up to $1.75 billion in debt.
Wolters Kluwer gained following some positive analyst comment on its cash flow development.
